title: Causal Interpretation of Arellano-Bond Coefficients under Treatment-History Coarsening in Binary Markov Panels
banked_reason: Math review passed; D0.5 field novelty floor failed because the general frontier is finite cone enumeration and the package lacks sampling selection and inference (paper score ceiling 5.8 < 7.4).
gap_reasons: Its broader frontier is delivered through finite matrix and cone enumeration; the compact structural classification applies only to mature full-degree blocks without prefix resets.

The causal interpretation builds on the selected-IV decomposition already developed by [Marx, Tamer, and Tang](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.19060v2), leaving a specialized dictionary classification as the contribution.
No sample procedure or inference establishes that the shortest dictionary can be selected reliably from data, and the rational examples provide limited evidence of practical relevance.
proof_attempt_summary: Seven D0 solve rounds produced a sound exact population lag-degree scan, mature-window cone structure, open 3-to-4-lag elbow, reset and early-date results, and audited rational certificates. The math panel passed with no findings, but the cold field-tier review rated the completed contribution incremental because the general frontier still uses finite cone enumeration and offers no sample selector or inference. Further sampling theory or a universal primitive elbow theorem would be a new project.
tldr: For full-support binary Markov panels with cumulative-dose current effects and untreated increments, a coefficientwise count-polynomial test decides every treatment-history lag and interaction dictionary for a convex causal Arellano--Bond-style coefficient with treatment-change normalization, period controls, and the lagged-outcome regressor retained. At every mature full-interaction window of length \(L\), the balanced space has dimension \(2^L-2L\), but effect weights and the retained-control moment depend on only \(2(L-2)\) primitive mass coordinates. A full-rank horizon-eight law strictly separates three-lag failure from four-lag success within the exact monotone frontier.
gap: Existing dynamic-panel causal decompositions show effect and trend contamination, while generic GMM work explains instrument weighting. Neither inspected line classifies cumulative-dose balance with a minimal treatment-history dictionary and the retained coefficient normalizations.
fill: Derive transition-and-contrast conditions, explicit positive switch scores, and matched-rank impossibility certificates for the feasible-pair set, including its lexicographically shortest lag window and degree whenever the set is nonempty.
